::: {.scope-note}
**Scope.** This is only the supported TREC RAG 2026 competition path. It does
not describe legacy baselines, development experiments, evaluation systems, or
every reusable package in the repository.
:::

The system performs two jobs in order. **Retrieval** finds and seals evidence.
Only after Retrieval finishes does **Generation** use that sealed evidence to
write an answer. That separation is the central architecture decision.

::: {.running-example}
### Illustrative narrative — not a TREC test topic

Imagine a friend asks: *How should a city protect outdoor workers and runners
during an extreme-heat week, including hydration, schedule changes, warning
signs, and interactions with poor air quality?*

We will follow this fictional information need through every figure. It is not
copied from the test set, and the examples below are not corpus text or a model
answer.
:::

## A small glossary {.unnumbered}

Narrative
: The complete official information need. It is broader than a short search
  query and remains the contract for the final answer.

Subnarrative
: A focused semantic slice proposed by the planner. It groups later evidence;
  it is not itself an executable search.

Query lane
: One executable search. The untouched narrative is always one lane. A
  successful plan contributes **1–3 BM25 query lanes per subnarrative**.

Document
: One ClimbMix source returned by Pyserini.

Chunk
: An overlapping piece cut from a document so a reranker can score manageable
  text windows.

Passage
: A scored chunk in a query-specific ranking.

Selected evidence
: An exact source span that passed local admission, deduplication, and diversity
  selection. It can ground the answer.

Canonical hint
: A Nuggetizer-produced claim-shaped summary linked to selected evidence. It
  helps organize coverage but is not independent factual authority.

Handoff
: The canonical, hash-authenticated file that freezes the only context
  Generation is allowed to read.

Citation
: A source document ID attached to an answer claim, later converted into the
  organizer's integer reference indexes.

::: {.visual-legend}
### How to read every image {.unnumbered}

- **Solid arrows** carry data, passages, selected evidence, or validated output.
- **Dashed arrows** carry advisory, bounded-control, failure, or retry flow.
- Folded-corner shapes are artifacts; cylinders are stores; diamonds are gates.
- Teal names Retrieval. Indigo names Generation. Labels and shapes repeat the
  meaning so the diagrams still work without color.
:::

# The whole system {#whole-system}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Retrieval and Generation are separate sealed stages. Only one
authenticated evidence handoff crosses between them.
:::

![The supported path begins with an official narrative, passes through Retrieval and one authenticated handoff, then reaches GPT-5.6 Sol Generation, local validation, and organizer RAG JSONL. Retrieval separately emits its run and full-text ZIP.](2026-competition-architecture/01-whole-system.svg){#fig-whole-system}

[Open the reusable whole-system SVG](2026-competition-architecture/01-whole-system.svg){.figure-source}

Retrieval can publish organizer evidence artifacts, but it does not pass those
artifacts into Generation. Generation receives a smaller, purpose-built
context: the selected passages and their authenticated provenance. This makes
the boundary inspectable and prevents later code from quietly expanding the
model's information access.

**Text equivalent:** The official narrative enters Retrieval. Retrieval emits
the official evidence run and full-text ZIP on one branch and an authenticated
selected-evidence handoff on the main branch. Only that handoff crosses the
Retrieval/Generation boundary. GPT-5.6 Sol produces structured answer objects,
which must pass local validation before becoming organizer RAG JSONL.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The supported commands and boundary are documented in
  [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) and the
  [competition README](../code/trec_rag/README.md).
- Retrieval is implemented by
  [`competition_retrieval.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_retrieval.py).
  Generation is implemented by
  [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py).
- This guide explains mechanics and contracts. It does not claim that answer
  quality, retrieval benefit, or entailment quality has been established.

</details>

# Retrieval: widen, score, then narrow {#retrieval}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Agentic retrieval here means bounded planning at the edge—not an
open-ended model that repeatedly searches until it decides to stop.
:::

![Retrieval preserves the original narrative query lane. Planning may add zero to eight subnarratives, each containing one to three BM25 query lanes. All one to twenty-five possible lanes use the same Pyserini and Mixedbread boundary before local evidence selection and optional Nuggetizer hints.](2026-competition-architecture/02-retrieval-system.svg){#fig-retrieval-system}

[Open the reusable Retrieval SVG](2026-competition-architecture/02-retrieval-system.svg){.figure-source}

For our heat-safety example, the original narrative searches as written. A
planner may also add narrower subnarratives for hydration, work scheduling,
warning signs, and heat-plus-air-quality guidance. Each successful
subnarrative contains one to three BM25 query strings. Those strings become
executable lanes; every lane crosses the same fixed retrieval boundary.

The prominent limits are per lane: [≤1,000 documents / focused query]{.limit}
enter from Pyserini, and [≤100 passages / focused query]{.limit} remain after
chunk scoring. The original lane plus up to eight subnarratives with three
queries each means **at most 25 searches per topic**. The 1,000 and 100 values
are independent per-query ceilings, not global topic totals.

**Text equivalent:** The official narrative creates one always-present query
lane. A valid plan has one to eight subnarratives, each with one to three BM25
queries; a failed plan adds none. The result is one to 25 executable query
lanes. Each searches ClimbMix through Pyserini, chunks returned documents, uses
Mixedbread to rank passages, and retains a query-specific top list. Local
selection creates factual passages. Nuggetizer optionally creates advisory
hints. Both are sealed into the handoff, while Retrieval also creates its
organizer-facing exports.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The checked-in
  [Retrieval config](../configs/rag26_competition_retrieval_v2.yaml) fixes
  `documents_per_query: 1000`, `passages_per_query: 100`, the
  `climbmix-400b` index, and the Mixedbread model.
- [`competition_retrieval.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_retrieval.py)
  orchestrates the stages. The fixed and agentic adapters call the same shared
  passage-search boundary described in
  [`code/trec_rag/README.md`](../code/trec_rag/README.md).
- “Agentic” is intentionally narrow: the hosted model decomposes the
  information need, while query execution, limits, ranking, evidence admission,
  checkpointing, and export remain deterministic or locally controlled.

</details>

# Planning is bounded {#planning}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** DeepSeek may widen the search, but it cannot replace the narrative
or start an unbounded plan–search–replan loop.
:::

![One strict DeepSeek V4 Flash call receives the full narrative. The original query lane remains. Zero to eight subnarratives may add one to three BM25 queries each, for at most twenty-four planned lanes and twenty-five total. Planning failure falls back to the original-only lane.](2026-competition-architecture/03-bounded-deepseek-planning.svg){#fig-bounded-planning}

[Open the reusable bounded-planning SVG](2026-competition-architecture/03-bounded-deepseek-planning.svg){.figure-source}

DeepSeek V4 Flash performs **bounded agentic planning**. It sees the complete
narrative once and returns a strict structured decomposition. In a valid
planner response it supplies one to eight subnarratives; across the whole system
there may therefore be **0–8 focused subnarratives**, because a failed plan
contributes none. Every successful subnarrative contains one to three BM25
queries, producing up to 24 planned query lanes. The untouched narrative is
never removed and supplies the twenty-fifth possible lane.

For the running example, “warning signs that require stopping exercise” can
become a subnarrative with short BM25 queries such as “heat illness stop
exercise warning signs.” The system—not the planner—owns when retrieval
happens, how much each query retrieves, and when it stops.

**Text equivalent:** One complete narrative goes to one strict DeepSeek planning
request. The original narrative becomes an unconditional Retrieval lane. A
valid plan contributes one to eight subnarratives, each holding one to three
BM25 queries. Those become up to 24 planned lanes, so the original-plus-planned
range is one to 25 searches. Every query crosses the fixed search boundary
once. If planning fails validation or transport, the system retains the
original-only lane and does not begin an iterative agent loop.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The figure uses the friendly name **DeepSeek V4 Flash**. The pinned route is
  `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-20260423` in
  [`facet_extraction.py`](../code/trec_rag/facet_extraction.py).
- That module fixes `MAX_SUBNARRATIVES = 8`, `MAX_BM25_QUERIES = 3`, strict JSON
  schema, temperature zero, seed zero, and disabled reasoning for this planning
  request.
- Planning failure behavior and the original-only fallback are enforced by
  [`competition_retrieval.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_retrieval.py), not
  left to the model.

</details>

# One query changes units {#candidate-accounting}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** “A thousand in, a hundred out” is shorthand. The system changes
from documents to chunks/passages between those two ceilings.
:::

![A conceptual funnel for one focused query starts with at most one thousand ClimbMix documents, changes units into overlapping chunks, ranks them with Mixedbread, and retains at most one hundred passages.](2026-competition-architecture/04-per-query-candidate-accounting.svg){#fig-candidate-accounting}

[Open the reusable candidate-accounting SVG](2026-competition-architecture/04-per-query-candidate-accounting.svg){.figure-source}

Pyserini asks the remote ClimbMix index for at most 1,000 **documents** for one
query. Each non-empty document is cut into overlapping **chunks**. Mixedbread
scores those chunks against that query, so the scored units are now called
**passages**. One global ranking keeps at most 100 passages for the lane.

The funnel is methodology, not measured volume: its widths are not proportional,
and a ceiling is not a target. A query may return fewer documents, a document
may produce a different number of chunks, and fewer than 100 eligible passages
may survive.

**Text equivalent:** For one focused query, Pyserini returns no more than 1,000
ClimbMix documents. Non-empty documents are divided into chunks no longer than
3500 characters with a 350-character overlap. Mixedbread scores every chunk as
a passage, and one query-wide ranking retains no more than 100 passages. The
same process repeats independently for the original narrative and each planned
lane.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- Exact configuration: `documents_per_query: 1000`,
  `chunk_max_characters: 3500`, `chunk_overlap_characters: 350`, and
  `passages_per_query: 100` in the
  [Retrieval config](../configs/rag26_competition_retrieval_v2.yaml).
- **Pyserini** is the retrieval API boundary; **ClimbMix** is the searched
  collection/index. The ranking model is **Mixedbread**, exact identifier
  `mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-base-v2`.
- A passage ranking is query-specific. It should not be described as 100 whole
  documents or as one top-100 list shared by all topic lanes.

</details>

# Evidence first; hints second {#evidence}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Selected passages are factual authority. Canonical claim hints are advisory.
:::

![Local exact-span selection creates factual selected passages. A dashed advisory branch sends those passages once through Nuggetizer to create bounded claim hints, while failure leaves the exact extractive evidence intact.](2026-competition-architecture/05-evidence-and-nuggetizer.svg){#fig-evidence-nuggetizer}

[Open the reusable evidence-and-Nuggetizer SVG](2026-competition-architecture/05-evidence-and-nuggetizer.svg){.figure-source}

The top passages are still candidates. Local code finds exact spans, ranks them
within the relevant subnarrative, removes duplicates, clusters for diversity,
and selects within a budget. These source-linked spans are what Generation may
use as facts.

The **Nuggetizer** package sees the selected passages and proposes a smaller set
of claim-shaped hints. A hint can tell Sol, “cover the relationship between heat
warning signs and stopping activity,” while its linked passages remain the
actual evidence. If canonicalization fails, deterministic exact extractive
evidence remains; the system does not promote an unsupported model claim.

**Text equivalent:** Query-ranked passages enter a local exact-span,
deduplication, diversity, and budget-selection stage. It selects at most 40
evidence items per subnarrative. A solid path carries those exact passages as
factual authority. A dashed path makes at most one hosted Nuggetizer call and
may create at most 20 advisory claim hints per subnarrative, with at most three
supporting documents per claim. Canonicalization failure leaves the exact
passages intact. The handoff contains both roles without equating them.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- The [Retrieval config](../configs/rag26_competition_retrieval_v2.yaml) fixes
  an evidence budget of 40, a claim limit of 20, and a supporting-document limit
  of 3 per subnarrative.
- [`canonical_nuggets.py`](../code/trec_rag/canonical_nuggets.py) wraps the
  Nuggetizer adapter as a one-shot bounded canonicalization stage. Package
  scoring is local; hosted scoring and assignment are bypassed.
- [`generation_handoff.py`](../code/trec_rag/generation_handoff.py) preserves
  selected evidence and claim hints as different typed records with linked
  provenance.

</details>

# The handoff is the trust boundary {#handoff}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Generation authenticates one purpose-built file. It is not allowed
to browse Retrieval's other outputs or evaluation material.
:::

![The generation handoff document contains narrative, evidence groups and passages, advisory hints, allowed citation IDs, source receipts, and hashes. Generation authenticates it, while five named artifacts are visibly barred.](2026-competition-architecture/06-generation-handoff-contract.svg){#fig-handoff-contract}

[Open the reusable handoff-contract SVG](2026-competition-architecture/06-generation-handoff-contract.svg){.figure-source}

`generation_handoff_manifest.json` is both a context package and an integrity
contract. It binds the exact narrative, selected evidence, advisory hints,
citation domain, and source receipts with canonical serialization and hashes.
Generation rejects malformed, contradictory, non-canonical, or unauthenticated
bytes instead of trying to “make them work.”

This boundary is also about absence. Generation never opens the **TREC run**,
**full-text ZIP**, **qrels**, **gold nuggets**, or **RAGDoll scores**. The first
two are Retrieval deliverables; the last three are evaluation or gold material.
None is an answer-generation input.

**Text equivalent:** Retrieval publishes one canonical handoff containing the
official narrative, selected evidence groups and exact passages, advisory claim
hints, allowed citation document IDs, source receipts, and hashes. A horizontal
trust boundary separates the stages. Generation authenticates and opens only
that manifest. The retrieval run, full-text ZIP, qrels, gold nuggets, and
RAGDoll scores are shown in a barred group with no edge into Generation.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- [`generation_handoff.py`](../code/trec_rag/generation_handoff.py) defines
  `generation_handoff_manifest_v1`, canonical JSON serialization, payload and
  context hashes, strict reconstruction, and authenticated loading.
- The handoff derives the allowed citation document IDs from selected evidence
  document identity and rank; it does not grant the model an arbitrary corpus
  lookup.
- [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py) accepts the
  handoff manifest as its only configured input path.

</details>

# Generation with GPT-5.6 Sol {#generation}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Sol receives a deterministic projection of the handoff, not a
retrieval tool and not the raw retrieval export.
:::

![The authenticated handoff becomes a deterministic prompt for GPT-5.6 Sol using medium reasoning, strict structured output, and a twelve-thousand-token ceiling. Sol returns answer objects with raw allowed document IDs.](2026-competition-architecture/07-sol-generation.svg){#fig-sol-generation}

[Open the reusable Sol-generation SVG](2026-competition-architecture/07-sol-generation.svg){.figure-source}

The Generation runner renders the narrative, selected passages, advisory hints,
and allowed document IDs into a fixed prompt. GPT-5.6 Sol is asked for strict
JSON answer objects, not free-form prose. Each object contains claim text and
raw ClimbMix document-ID citations drawn from the handoff's allowed domain.

For our fictional narrative, Sol could organize an answer across hydration,
schedule changes, warning signs, and air quality—but every asserted answer
object still needs selected-passage support and allowed citations. The diagram
shows configuration, not a claim about the quality of a hypothetical answer.

**Text equivalent:** The authenticated handoff enters a deterministic prompt
projection. That prompt supplies factual selected passages, advisory coverage
hints, and allowed document IDs to GPT-5.6 Sol. The model uses medium reasoning,
strict structured output, and a 12,000-token ceiling. It returns answer objects
with claim text and one to three raw ClimbMix document IDs for local validation;
they are not organizer integer indexes yet.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- Friendly figure label: **GPT-5.6 Sol**. Exact configured route:
  `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` in the
  [Generation config](../configs/rag26_competition_rag_gpt_sol_v2.yaml).
- The same config fixes `reasoning_effort: medium`,
  `structured_output: strict_schema`, `max_tokens: 12000`, and generation
  concurrency 4.
- [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py) renders the prompt,
  defines the strict response schema, and writes raw provider responses only to
  private work state—not to this report.

</details>

# Validation has two retry clocks {#validation}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Transport retries deliver one request; semantic retries give a
topic one more chance to produce locally valid meaning. They are not six generic
model retries.
:::

![A semantic-attempt boundary contains the hosted request and local validation. The request has at most three transport attempts, while the topic has at most two semantic attempts. Accepted document IDs are converted deterministically to organizer indexes.](2026-competition-architecture/08-validation-and-retries.svg){#fig-validation-retries}

[Open the reusable validation-and-retries SVG](2026-competition-architecture/08-validation-and-retries.svg){.figure-source}

The transport clock handles delivery failures such as a retryable network or
provider error. One semantic attempt can therefore contain [≤3 transport attempts]{.limit}.
After a response arrives, local code validates its meaning
and organizer contract. A retryable semantic failure can trigger one revised
prompt, for [≤2 semantic attempts]{.limit} total.

The gate checks strict structure, the **1,024-word ceiling**, citation count and
uniqueness, membership in the handoff's citation domain, and knowable
claim-hint-to-document compatibility. After acceptance, deterministic code
prunes uncited references and remaps raw document IDs to organizer integer
indexes without rewriting answer text.

**Text equivalent:** A topic-level box allows at most two semantic attempts. In
each attempt, the hosted generation request has at most three transport
attempts. The returned answer passes a local diamond-shaped gate checking strict
schema, no more than 1,024 words, one to three unique allowed citations per
answer object, and exact-hint compatibility. A retryable semantic failure loops
once to a revised prompt. Accepted raw document IDs then pass through
deterministic reference pruning and citation-index conversion to form an
organizer-valid row.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- `transport_max_attempts: 3` comes from the
  [Generation config](../configs/rag26_competition_rag_gpt_sol_v2.yaml).
  `MAX_SEMANTIC_ATTEMPTS = 2` is fixed in
  [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py).
- The semantic retry instruction is added only after a retryable local semantic
  failure. Non-retryable failures stop early rather than spending the full
  budget.
- Citation normalization derives the final reference list from citations that
  survived validation. Invalid or fabricated citations are rejected, not
  silently dropped.

</details>

# Two organizer-facing outputs {#outputs}

::: {.takeaway}
**Takeaway:** Retrieval and Generation publish different deliverables. The
handoff connects the commands; the Retrieval run and ZIP do not.
:::

![Competition Retrieval publishes an evidence run, full-text ZIP, export receipt, and the selected-evidence handoff. Only the handoff enters GPT-5.6 Sol Generation, which publishes organizer RAG JSONL.](2026-competition-architecture/09-organizer-output-split.svg){#fig-output-split}

[Open the reusable organizer-output SVG](2026-competition-architecture/09-organizer-output-split.svg){.figure-source}

The first command publishes the organizer's evidence ranking and required
full-text archive, sealed by a manifest-last receipt. It also publishes the
private Generation handoff. The second command authenticates that handoff and
publishes `rag_output_trec_rag_2026.jsonl`, the organizer RAG JSONL.

This is why “Retrieval then Generation” is more precise than drawing one large
undifferentiated RAG box. The stages have different inputs, different failure
modes, different outputs, and a deliberately narrow contract between them.

**Text equivalent:** Competition Retrieval publishes three sibling organizer
artifacts—the official TREC evidence run, full-text ZIP, and export receipt—and
also publishes the authenticated Generation handoff. A stop notice says the run
and ZIP are never Generation inputs. Only the handoff crosses the boundary into
GPT-5.6 Sol Generation. Generation publishes the organizer RAG JSONL containing
validated answers and deterministic citation indexes.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes and sources</summary>

- Retrieval output names are `r_output_trec_rag_2026.tsv`,
  `retrieval_with_text.jsonl.zip`, and `retrieval_export_manifest.json`, as
  documented in [`code/trec_rag/README.md`](../code/trec_rag/README.md).
- Generation's configured output is `rag_output_trec_rag_2026.jsonl` in
  [`competition_rag.py`](../code/trec_rag/competition_rag.py).
- The handoff is private pipeline state. This report contains only the contract
  and fictional examples, never a live handoff, output row, or corpus passage.

</details>

# Sources and scope {#sources}

This guide was mechanically grounded at merge commit `7e9d3b9` in the checked-in
configs and modules linked above. The canonical authored source is
[`reports/2026-competition-architecture.qmd`](2026-competition-architecture.qmd);
the page you are reading is its generated, self-contained HTML rendering. The
nine reusable figures and their provenance map live in
[`reports/2026-competition-architecture/`](2026-competition-architecture/README.md).

What is verified here: stage order, limits, identities, data contracts, failure
paths, validation, and artifact ownership. What remains unknown: how well the
configured system will retrieve evidence or answer the official topics until
it is run and evaluated under the competition protocol.
